  - [67]{.lawlabel} Sections 435 and 436 of the Regulations are replaced
    by the following:

    :::: section
    ::: AmendedText
    - ###### Application of former Regulations {#application-of-former-regulations .MarginalNote}

      - [434.1]{.lawlabel} [(1)]{.lawlabel} Sections 4, 5, 424 and 430
        to 444 of the former Regulations continue to apply in respect of
        a lamp that is

        - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a [[CFL]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef}, as defined
          in section 430 of the former Regulations, manufactured before
          January 1, 2027;

        - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a [[general service
          lamp]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef}, as defined in subsection 433(1)
          of the former Regulations, manufactured before January 1,
          2026;

        - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a [[modified spectrum incandescent
          lamp]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef}, as defined in section 437 of the
          former Regulations, manufactured before January 1, 2026; or

        - [(d)]{.lawlabel} a [[general service incandescent reflector
          lamp]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef}, as defined in section 441 of the
          former Regulations, manufactured before January 1, 2026.

      - ###### Non-application --- early compliance {#non-application-early-compliance .MarginalNote}

        [(2)]{.lawlabel} Subsection (1) does not apply in respect of a
        lamp that is deemed, under section 436.1, to satisfy the
        requirements of sections 4, 5, 435 and 436.

    - ###### Energy efficiency standards {#energy-efficiency-standards-1 .MarginalNote}

      - [435]{.lawlabel} [(1)]{.lawlabel} The energy efficiency
        standards set out in TSD D7SB001 apply to general service lamps.

      - ###### Testing standard {#testing-standard-2 .MarginalNote}

        [(2)]{.lawlabel} A general service lamp complies with the energy
        efficiency standard if it meets that standard when tested in
        accordance with the applicable testing procedures established by
        10 C.F.R. §430.23(gg).

    - ###### Information {#information .MarginalNote}

      [436]{.lawlabel} For the purposes of subsection 5(1) of the Act,
      the following information must be provided to the Minister in
      respect of a general service lamp:

      - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a description of the lamp, collected in
        accordance with ANSI C78.79; and

      - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the following information, collected in
        accordance with 10 C.F.R. §430.23(gg):

        - [(i)]{.lawlabel} the rated lumen output or, in the case of a
          three-way lamp, the three rated lumen outputs, in lumens,

        - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the rated power or, in the case of a
          three-way lamp, the three values for rated power, in watts,

        - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the rated lamp efficacy, in lm/W,

        - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} the rated life, in hours,

        - [(v)]{.lawlabel} the rated correlated colour temperature or
          range of correlated colour temperatures, in degrees Kelvin,
          and

        - [(vi)]{.lawlabel} the rated colour rendering index.
    :::
    ::::

  - - [68]{.lawlabel} [(2)]{.lawlabel} Section 436.1 of the Regulations

      :::: section

      - ###### Early compliance {#early-compliance-5 .MarginalNote}

        [436.1]{.lawlabel} A general service lamp is deemed to satisfy
        the requirements of sections 4, 5, 435 and 436 if

        - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a general service incandescent
          lamp or general service incandescent reflector lamp, it was

          2026 and satisfies the requirements of sections 4, 5, 435 and
          436 that would have applied to the lamp if it had been
          manufactured on or after January 1, 2026; and

        - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in any other case, it was manufactured on or
          after January 1, 2025 and before January 1, 2027 and satisfies
          the requirements of sections 4, 5, 435 and 436 that would have
          applied to the lamp if it had been manufactured on or after
          January 1, 2027.
      :::

- --- SOR/2025-110, s. 70

  - [70]{.lawlabel} The reference "\[594 to 634 reserved\]" after
    section 593 of the Regulations is replaced by the following:

    :::: section
    ::: AmendedText
    ##### [SUBDIVISION F]{.HLabel3}[Line Voltage Thermostats]{.HTitleText3} {#subdivision-fline-voltage-thermostats .SchedHeadL3}

    - ###### Definitions {#definitions-1 .MarginalNote}

      - [594]{.lawlabel} [(1)]{.lawlabel} The following definitions
        apply in this Subdivision.

        [[control point]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

        :   [[control point]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means the temperature
            value, measured at the centre of the test room, that is used
            to verify the performance of a line voltage thermostat at
            the set point. ([température de contrôle]{.DefinedTermLink
            lang="fr"})

        [[CSA C828-19]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

        :   [[CSA C828-19]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means the CSA standard
            CSA C828:19 entitled Performance requirements for line
            voltage thermostats used with individual room electric space
            heating devices. ([CSA C828-19]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

        [[differential]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

        :   [[differential]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means the difference
            between the maximum and minimum air temperatures at the
            centre of the test room, calculated at 50% duty
            cycle. ([différentielle]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

        [[droop]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

        :   [[droop]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means the difference between
            the minimum air temperatures at the centre of the test room,
            calculated at 20% and 80% duty cycle,
            respectively. ([dérive]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

        [[line voltage thermostat]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

        :   [[line voltage thermostat]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means,
            subject to subsection (2), a thermostat that is used with a
            line voltage of between 120 V and 240 V, is intended for
            switching of a controlled resistive heating load and is one
            of the following:

            - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a wall-mounted thermostat designed to be
              used with baseboards, panel convectors or radiant floors;

            - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a built-in thermostat having a nominal
              load from 1000 W to 1500 W that is used in baseboards or
              panel convectors; or

            - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a two-component thermostat. ([thermostat
              à tension de secteur]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

      - ###### Exclusion --- definition of [[line voltage thermostat]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef} {#exclusion-definition-of-line-voltage-thermostat .MarginalNote}

        [(2)]{.lawlabel} The definition [[line voltage
        thermostat]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef} in subsection (1) does not
        include thermostats designed to be used exclusively for or built
        into

        - [(a)]{.lawlabel} fan-forced heaters;

        - [(b)]{.lawlabel} kick space heaters;

        - [(c)]{.lawlabel} fireplaces;

        - [(d)]{.lawlabel} thermal storage heaters;

        - [(e)]{.lawlabel} electric baseboards and convectors
          incorporating both convection and radiant heating elements;

        - [(f)]{.lawlabel} portable heaters; or

        - [(g)]{.lawlabel} central heating units under the control of a
          single thermostat.

    - ###### Energy-using product {#energy-using-product .MarginalNote}

      - [595]{.lawlabel} [(1)]{.lawlabel} A line voltage thermostat is
        prescribed as an energy-using product.

      - ###### Limit {#limit-2 .MarginalNote}

        [(2)]{.lawlabel} However, for the purposes of sections 4, 5, 596
        and 597, a line voltage thermostat is not considered to be an
        energy-using product unless

        - [(a)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a wall-mounted thermostat or a
          two-component thermostat, it is manufactured on or after July
          1, 2026; and

        - [(b)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a built-in thermostat, it is
          manufactured on or after July 1, 2027.

    - ###### Energy efficiency standards {#energy-efficiency-standards-2 .MarginalNote}

      - [596]{.lawlabel} [(1)]{.lawlabel} The energy efficiency
        standards set out in clause 4.4 of CSA C828-19 apply to a line
        voltage thermostat.

      - ###### Testing standard {#testing-standard-3 .MarginalNote}

        [(2)]{.lawlabel} A line voltage thermostat complies with the
        energy efficiency standard when tested in accordance with the
        applicable testing procedures established by CSA C828-19.

    - ###### Information {#information-1 .MarginalNote}

      [597]{.lawlabel} For the purpose of subsection 5(1) of the Act,
      the following information must be collected in accordance with CSA
      C828-19 and provided to the Minister in respect of a line voltage
      thermostat:

      - [(a)]{.lawlabel} its equipment class;

      - [(b)]{.lawlabel} its nominal voltage;

      - [(c)]{.lawlabel} its maximum nominal load, expressed in watts;

      - [(d)]{.lawlabel} its minimum nominal load, expressed in watts;

      - [(e)]{.lawlabel} its droop, expressed in degrees Celsius;

      - [(f)]{.lawlabel} its differential, expressed in degrees Celsius;
        and

      - [(g)]{.lawlabel} its control point precision, expressed in
        degrees Celsius.

    \[598 to 634 reserved\]
    :::
    ::::

- --- SOR/2025-110, s. 75

  - [75]{.lawlabel} The Regulations are amended by adding the following
    after section 803:

    :::: section
    ::: AmendedText
    ##### [SUBDIVISION B]{.HLabel3}[Faucets]{.HTitleText3} {#subdivision-bfaucets .SchedHeadL3}

    - ###### Definitions {#definitions-3 .MarginalNote}

      [803.1]{.lawlabel} The following definitions apply in this
      Subdivision.

      [[faucet]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

      :   [[faucet]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means

          - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a private lavatory faucet;

          - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a replacement aerator for a private
            lavatory faucet;

          - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a public lavatory faucet;

          - [(d)]{.lawlabel} a replacement aerator for a public lavatory
            faucet;

          - [(e)]{.lawlabel} a kitchen faucet, other than one that is
            designed and marketed exclusively for use in industrial,
            commercial or institutional kitchens;

          - [(f)]{.lawlabel} a replacement aerator for a kitchen faucet,
            other than one that is designed and marketed exclusively for
            use in industrial, commercial or institutional kitchens; or

          - [(g)]{.lawlabel} a metering faucet. 

          It does not include a faucet that is designed and marketed
          exclusively for use in health care facilities, a low-pressure
          water dispenser or a pot filler. ([robinet]{.DefinedTermLink
          lang="fr"})

      [[low-pressure water dispenser]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

      :   [[low-pressure water dispenser]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a
          terminal fitting that dispenses drinking water at a pressure
          of 105 kPa (15 psi) or less. ([distributeur d'eau à basse
          pression]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

      [[pot filler]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

      :   [[pot filler]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a terminal fitting
          that can accommodate only a single supply water inlet, with an
          articulated arm or the equivalent that allows the product to
          reach to fill vessels when in use and allows the product to be
          retracted when not in use. ([robinet
          remplisseur]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

    - ###### Energy-using product {#energy-using-product-1 .MarginalNote}

      - [803.2]{.lawlabel} [(1)]{.lawlabel} A faucet is prescribed as an
        energy-using product.

      - ###### Limit {#limit-3 .MarginalNote}

        [(2)]{.lawlabel} However, for the purposes of sections 4, 5 and
        803.3, a faucet is not considered to be an energy-using product
        unless it is manufactured on or after July 1, 2026.

    - ###### Energy efficiency standards {#energy-efficiency-standards-3 .MarginalNote}

      - [803.3]{.lawlabel} [(1)]{.lawlabel} The energy efficiency
        standards set out in column 2 of the table to this section apply
        to faucets described in column 1.

      - ###### Testing standard {#testing-standard-4 .MarginalNote}

        [(2)]{.lawlabel} A faucet complies with the energy efficiency
        standard if it meets that standard when tested in accordance
        with the applicable testing procedures established by 10 C.F.R.
        Appendix S.

      [803.4]{.lawlabel} For the purpose of subsection 5(1) of the Act,
      the following information must be collected in accordance with 10
      C.F.R. Appendix S and provided to the Minister in respect of a
      faucet:

      - [(a)]{.lawlabel} its type;

      - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the maximum water flow rate, expressed in
        litres per cycle (US gallons per cycle) for metering faucets and
        in litres per minute (US gallons per minute) for other faucets;

      - [(c)]{.lawlabel} if the product is a kitchen faucet with the
        capacity for temporary flow rate increase, the maximum flow rate
        of that temporary flow, expressed in litres per minute (US
        gallons per minute), in addition to the information referred to
        in paragraph (b); and

      - [(d)]{.lawlabel} the water pressure at which the maximum water
        flow rate was measured, expressed in kPa (psi).

    ##### [SUBDIVISION C]{.HLabel3}[Showerheads]{.HTitleText3} {#subdivision-cshowerheads .SchedHeadL3}

    - Definition of [[showerhead]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

      [803.5]{.lawlabel} In this Subdivision,
      [[showerhead]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a component or set of
      components with one or multiple nozzles that is intended for
      attachment to a single supply fitting for spraying water onto a
      bather. It does not include a showerhead designed and marketed
      exclusively for the emergency washing of a person who has been
      exposed to hazardous materials or a showerhead designed and
      marketed exclusively for use in health care facilities.

    - ###### Energy-using product {#energy-using-product-2 .MarginalNote}

      - [803.6]{.lawlabel} [(1)]{.lawlabel} A showerhead is prescribed
        as an energy-using product.

      - ###### Limit {#limit-4 .MarginalNote}

        [(2)]{.lawlabel} However, for the purposes of sections 4, 5 and
        803.7, a showerhead is not considered to be an energy-using
        product unless it is manufactured on or after July 1, 2026.

    - ###### Energy efficiency standard {#energy-efficiency-standard-1 .MarginalNote}

      - [803.7]{.lawlabel} [(1)]{.lawlabel} The energy efficiency
        standards set out in column 2 of the table to this section apply
        to showerheads described in column 1. For showerheads with
        multiple nozzles, the maximum water flow rate applies regardless
        of the number of nozzles in use.

      - ###### Testing standard {#testing-standard-5 .MarginalNote}

        [(2)]{.lawlabel} A showerhead complies with the energy
        efficiency standard if it meets that standard when tested in
        accordance with the applicable testing procedures established by
        10 C.F.R. Appendix S.

    ##### [SUBDIVISION B]{.HLabel3}[Pool Pumps]{.HTitleText3} {#subdivision-bpool-pumps .SchedHeadL3}

    - ###### Definitions {#definitions-4 .MarginalNote}

      - [808]{.lawlabel} [(1)]{.lawlabel} The following definitions
        apply in this Subdivision.

        [[10 C.F.R. §431.465(f)]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

        :   [[10 C.F.R. §431.465(f)]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means the
            table to paragraph (f) of section 431.465 of Subpart Y, Part
            431 of Title 10 to the United States Code of Federal
            Regulations, as amended from time to time. ([10 C.F.R.
            §431.465(f)]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

        [[10 C.F.R. §431.465(g)]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

        :   [[10 C.F.R. §431.465(g)]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means
            paragraph (g) of section 431.465 of Subpart Y, Part 431 of
            Title 10 to the United States Code of Federal Regulations,
            as amended from time to time. ([10 C.F.R.
            §431.465(g)]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

        [[10 C.F.R. §431.465(h)]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

        :   [[10 C.F.R. §431.465(h)]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means
            paragraph (h) of section 431.465 of Subpart Y, Part 431 of
            Title 10 to the United States Code of Federal Regulations,
            as amended from time to time. ([10 C.F.R.
            §431.465(h)]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"}) 

        [[10 C.F.R. Appendix C]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

        :   [[10 C.F.R. Appendix C]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means Appendix
            C to Subpart Y, Part 431 of Title 10 to the United States
            Code of Federal Regulations, entitled Uniform Test Method
            for the Measurement of Energy Efficiency of
            Dedicated-Purpose Pool Pumps, as amended from time to
            time. ([appendice C 10 C.F.R.]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

        [[pool pump]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

        :   [[pool pump]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means, subject to
            subsection (2), a pump that is designed for use with a pool
            or spa and that is

            - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a filter pump that has a hydraulic power
              of less than 1.865 kW (2.5 HP);

            - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a pressure cleaner booster pump;

            - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a waterfall pump with a maximum head less
              than or equal to 9.144 m (30 ft) and a maximum speed less
              than or equal to 1800 RPM;

            - [(d)]{.lawlabel} a pump with an integral sand filter;

            - [(e)]{.lawlabel} a pump with an integral cartridge filter;

            - [(f)]{.lawlabel} a pump for a storable electric spa; or

            - [(g)]{.lawlabel} a pump for a rigid electric spa. ([pompe
              de piscine]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

      - ###### Exclusion --- definition of [[pool pump]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef} {#exclusion-definition-of-pool-pump .MarginalNote}

        [(2)]{.lawlabel} The definition [[pool
        pump]{.dfn}]{.DefinitionRef} in subsection (1) does not include

        - [(a)]{.lawlabel} a clean water pump;

        - [(b)]{.lawlabel} a circulator pump;

        - [(c)]{.lawlabel} a submersible pump;

        - [(d)]{.lawlabel} a pool filter pump with hydraulic output
          power equal to or greater than 1.865 kW (2.5 HP); or

        - [(e)]{.lawlabel} a pump marketed exclusively for commercial
          use that has

          - [(i)]{.lawlabel} an orifice on the pump body that accepts
            suction side plumbing connections that has an inner diameter
            greater than 72 mm (2.85 inches), and

          - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} a measured performance greater than or
            equal to 757 litres per minute (200 US gallons per minute)
            at 15.24 m (50 feet) of head.

    - ###### Energy-using product {#energy-using-product-3 .MarginalNote}

      - [809]{.lawlabel} [(1)]{.lawlabel} A pool pump is prescribed as
        an energy-using product.

      - ###### Limit {#limit-5 .MarginalNote}

        [(2)]{.lawlabel} However, for the purposes of sections 4, 5 and
        810, a pool pump is not considered to be an energy-using product
        unless it is manufactured on or after January 1, 2026.

    - ###### Energy efficiency standards {#energy-efficiency-standards-4 .MarginalNote}

      - [810]{.lawlabel} [(1)]{.lawlabel} The energy efficiency
        standards set out in column 3 of the table to this section apply
        to pool pumps described in column 1.

      - ###### Testing standard {#testing-standard-6 .MarginalNote}

        [(2)]{.lawlabel} A pool pump complies with the energy efficiency
        standard if it meets that standard when tested in accordance
        with the applicable testing procedures established by the
        standard, if any, set out in column 2 of the table to this
        section.

    - ###### Information {#information-4 .MarginalNote}

      [811]{.lawlabel} For the purpose of subsection 5(1) of the Act,
      the following information must be provided to the Minister in
      respect of a pool pump:

      - [(a)]{.lawlabel} its type;

      - [(b)]{.lawlabel} its nominal motor power, expressed in watts;

      - [(c)]{.lawlabel} its nominal hydraulic power, expressed in
        watts;

      - [(d)]{.lawlabel} its total power, expressed in watts;

      - [(e)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a self-priming pool filter pump,
        a non-self-priming pool filter pump, a waterfall pump or a
        pressure cleaner booster pump, its weighted energy factor;

      - [(f)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a pool pump with an integral
        filter, information that indicates whether it has a separate or
        built-in timer;

      - [(g)]{.lawlabel} information that indicates whether it has
        freeze protection controls;

      - [(h)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a pool pump with freeze
        protection controls, information that indicates whether freeze
        protection is enabled or disabled; and

      - [(i)]{.lawlabel} in the case of a pool pump with freeze
        protection controls that are enabled, its default dry-bulb air
        temperature setting, default run-time and default motor speed.

    #### [DIVISION 15]{.HLabel2}[Air Compressors]{.HTitleText2} {#division-15air-compressors .SchedHeadL2}

    - ###### Definitions {#definitions-5 .MarginalNote}

      [812]{.lawlabel} The following definitions apply in this Division.

      [[10 C.F.R. §431.345]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

      :   [[10 C.F.R. §431.345]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means the table to
          section 431.345 to Subpart T, Part 431 of Title 10 to the
          United States Code of Federal Regulations, as amended from
          time to time. ([10 C.F.R. §431.345]{.DefinedTermLink
          lang="fr"})

      [[10 C.F.R. Appendix A]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

      :   [[10 C.F.R. Appendix A]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means Appendix A
          to Subpart T, Part 431 of Title 10 to the United States Code
          of Federal Regulations, entitled Uniform Test Method for
          Certain Air Compressors, as amended from time to
          time. ([appendice A 10 C.F.R.]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

      [[air compressor]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

      :   [[air compressor]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a lubricated
          rotary compressor that is designed to compress air, has an
          inlet open to the atmosphere or another source of air, is made
          up of one or more compression elements (bare compressors), one
          or more drivers, mechanical equipment to drive the compression
          elements and any ancillary equipment and has all of the
          following features:

          - [(a)]{.lawlabel} it is driven by a brushless three-phase
            electric motor;

          - [(b)]{.lawlabel} it is air- or liquid-cooled;

          - [(c)]{.lawlabel} it is fixed- or variable-speed;

          - [(d)]{.lawlabel} it has a full-load operating pressure that
            is greater than or equal to 0.52 MPa (75 psig) and less than
            or equal to 1.38 MPa (200 psig);

          - [(e)]{.lawlabel} it has a full-load actual volume flow rate
            that is greater than or equal to 0.99 m^3^/min (35 cfm) or
            has a motor whose nominal power is greater than or equal to
            7.46 kW (10 HP); and

          - [(f)]{.lawlabel} it has a full-load actual volume flow rate
            that is less than or equal to 35.4 m^3^/min (1250 cfm) or is
            sold or supplied with a compressor motor whose nominal power
            is less than or equal to 149.14 kW (200 HP).

          It does not include a liquid ring compressor, a reciprocating
          compressor or a rotary-type positive displacement compressor
          for use in the petroleum, petrochemical or natural gas
          industries. ([compresseur d'air]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

      [[compressor]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm}

      :   [[compressor]{.dfn}]{.DefinedTerm} means a machine or
          apparatus that converts different types of energy into the
          potential energy of gas pressure for displacement and
          compression of gaseous media to any pressure value above
          atmospheric pressure and has a pressure ratio at full-load
          operating pressure greater than
          1.3. ([compresseur]{.DefinedTermLink lang="fr"})

    - ###### Energy-using product {#energy-using-product-4 .MarginalNote}

      - [813]{.lawlabel} [(1)]{.lawlabel} An air compressor is
        prescribed as an energy-using product.

      - ###### Limit {#limit-6 .MarginalNote}

        [(2)]{.lawlabel} However, for the purposes of sections 4, 5 and
        814, an air compressor is not considered to be an energy-using
        product unless it is manufactured on or after July 1, 2026.

    - ###### Energy efficiency standard {#energy-efficiency-standard-2 .MarginalNote}

      - [814]{.lawlabel} [(1)]{.lawlabel} The energy efficiency standard
        that applies to an air compressor is the minimum package
        isentropic efficiency set out for the applicable equipment class
        in 10 C.F.R. §431.345.

      - ###### Testing standard {#testing-standard-7 .MarginalNote}

        [(2)]{.lawlabel} An air compressor complies with the energy
        efficiency standard if it meets that standard when tested in
        accordance with the applicable testing procedures established by
        10 C.F.R. Appendix A.

    - ###### Information {#information-5 .MarginalNote}

      [815]{.lawlabel} For the purpose of subsection 5(1) of the Act,
      the following information must be collected in accordance with 10
      C.F.R. Appendix A and provided to the Minister in respect of an
      air compressor:

      - [(a)]{.lawlabel} its equipment class;

      - [(b)]{.lawlabel} the air compressor motor nominal power,
        expressed in kilowatts (HP);

      - [(c)]{.lawlabel} its dimensionless full-load package isentropic
        efficiency or part-load package isentropic efficiency, as
        applicable;

      - [(d)]{.lawlabel} its full-load actual volume flow rate,
        expressed in m^3^/min (cfm);

      - [(e)]{.lawlabel} its full-load operating pressure, expressed in
        MPa (psig);

      - [(f)]{.lawlabel} its maximum full-flow operating pressure,
        expressed in MPa (psig);

      - [(g)]{.lawlabel} its pressure ratio at full-load operating
        pressure; and

      - [(h)]{.lawlabel} if any ancillary equipment that is not part of
        the air compressor package is installed for testing,

        - [(i)]{.lawlabel} a description of the ancillary equipment,

        - [(ii)]{.lawlabel} the manufacturer of the ancillary equipment
          and, if it is different than the manufacturer, the brand,

        - [(iii)]{.lawlabel} the model number of the ancillary
          equipment,

        - [(iv)]{.lawlabel} the serial number of the ancillary
          equipment, if any, and

        - [(v)]{.lawlabel} the input voltage, number of phases and input
          frequency of the ancillary equipment, if applicable.

The instruction for this value states “Replace “DDD” with single-duct and dual-duct portable air conditioners.” Next below, at the left margin, is the heading “Model number”. The value “FFF”, which is related to this heading, is centered on the graphic. The instruction for this value states “Replace “FFF” with model number.” Lastly, the graphic provides a reminder that “Removal of this label before first retail purchase is an offence (S.C. 1992, c. 36)”." />
    </div>
    </figure>
